courses.title: HTML Basics
courses.subtitle: Learn structure of web pages easily.

sections.title: Introduction:
sections.text: HTML, short for HyperText Markup Language, is the standard markup language used to create and structure content on the web. It serves as the backbone of every webpage by defining elements such as headings, paragraphs, links, images, and forms.

sections.title: What is HTML
sections.text: HTML is not a programming language, but a markup language that tells browsers how to display content. Each piece of content is wrapped in tags that describe its purpose. The current specification is the HTML Living Standard, maintained by WHATWG and updated continuously rather than in numbered versions.

sections.title: Purpose of HTML
sections.text: The primary goal of HTML is to structure content meaningfully so users, browsers, assistive technology, and search engines all understand what each section represents.

sections.title: HTML Document Structure Guidelines
sections.text: Every HTML document begins with a root <html> element. Inside it, two main sections exist: <head> for metadata and <body> for visible content.

sections.title: Head Section Guidelines
sections.text: The <head> section usually contains title tags, meta descriptions, charset settings, viewport configuration, and links to CSS/JS files. Metadata here is essential for browser behavior, social sharing previews, and SEO optimization.

courses.title: CSS Styling

sections.title: Introduction:
sections.text: CSS, or Cascading Style Sheets, controls how HTML elements look and behave on screen. It handles colors, spacing, typography, layout, and responsive design.

sections.title: What is CSS
sections.text: CSS separates presentation from structure, allowing developers to style many pages consistently from a single stylesheet. Modern CSS also handles logic that once required JavaScript, like responsive layout and simple state-based styling.

sections.title: Why CSS Matters
sections.text: Well-structured CSS keeps large codebases maintainable, ensures a consistent visual language, and directly impacts performance and accessibility through render efficiency and color contrast.

sections.title: What is JavaScript
sections.text: JavaScript is a dynamic, multi-paradigm language that runs in browsers, on servers via Node.js, and even on embedded devices. It evolves yearly through ECMAScript (ES) specifications, adding new syntax and built-in capabilities.

sections.title: Why JavaScript Matters
